LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST, IMITATIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: LISTENING AND SPEAKING Theme 9: Getting Around: At home
Topic 1.9: Listening for gist, Imitative speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for gist, Imitative speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we ensure we get the main ideas from listening to text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify general information from listening texts for comprehension
2. appreciate the role articulation plays in language

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR GIST, IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for gist, Imitative speaking helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR GIST, IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify general information from listening texts for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify general information from listening texts for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify general information from listening texts for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for gist, Imitative speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify general information from listening texts for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role articulation plays in language

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role articulation plays in language. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role articulation plays in language.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for gist, Imitative speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role articulation plays in language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for gist, Imitative speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for gist, Imitative speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify general information from listening texts for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for gist, Imitative speaking to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role articulation plays in language)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for gist, Imitative speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify general information from listening texts for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role articulation plays in language.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for gist, Imitative speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for gist, Imitative speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Listening for gist, Imitative speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we ensure we get the main ideas from listening to text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for gist, Imitative speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify general information from listening texts for comprehension.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role articulation plays in language.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
